findings.claim_text: Hyperliquid's own documentation says `l2Book` is "pushed on each block that is at least 0.5 since last push," and that `bbo` is sent only if the best bid or offer changes on a block.

Glassnode measured that path in March 2026 by placing 120 real market orders from AWS Tokyo: a median order-to-fill of 884 ms, range 695–1,634 ms, of which about 5 ms was network and about 879 ms processing (an estimate).
The inference: a p90 of 2–8 bp cannot be mostly stale-quote drift on a BTC-like asset, because a median stale frame is worth a fifth of a basis point and even a one-second frame under one.
findings.contradicting_quote: Arbitrageurs spam IOC orders speculatively, targeting expected stale liquidity. Block N commits at ~200-300 ms. Block N+1 commits at ~500-700 ms.
